title: Train travel versus band bus
summary: He says there is no comparison; buses lacked restrooms, and Harry Carney loved driving.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Of course, you also probably had less hectic schedules in those days when you had to depend -- yet they were dictated by train schedules rather than in later years where you took a plane had to play, and then you took the bus and --
Oh well, I don't know how I would say that. It just depended on when we had to get to the next job and -- that we would take -- how long we would keep these cars and things.
From your description of your own sleeper and your own dining car, it sounds a far cry from what I saw when I rode the bus.
Oh, yes. Yes.
In 1958 when you -- it was Howard Johnsons in the middle of the night, if it was a Howard Johnsons --
Right.
-- and the bus was what? Hot in the back and cold in the front.
Oh, you know for many years we had buses that didn't even have a restroom on them.
Yeah, well there was --
-- and they'd have to pick their stops and everything like that. Very bad.
I can remember the bus from here to San Francisco -- I believe it was in 1950 with the band -- and there was trouble finding a restroom that would accomodate the band in a small town.
Right.
And that was probably a problem, wasn't it?
Quite often. Quite often. Would you believe it? One time I rode a bus all the way from Seattle, Washington to New York City.
Mm.
Yeah, straight through.
That's -- that's the band bus?

Yeah. Yeah. We had a driver that could stay up looked like forever. And, of course, I wouldn't do it now because the danger wasn't as -- I wasn't conscious of the danger like I am now. But the -- imagine a man sitting at the wheel 12, 15 hours.
Bad as Harry Carney (unintelligible), huh?
Yeah, he used to like to do that too.
He used to play, when I was on the road with the band we would play a date and then get on the bus, and the band would sleep on the bus --
Yes.
-- until maybe noon the next day.

We'd get to the next destination and then get out, check into a hotel, and maybe get to sleep, (but) probably not. You'd just change your clothes and go to the job. Harry Carney would have been driving all that time, and then he'd go play.
Yes.
He must have been (inaudible). never slept,
Well, he was just crazy about driving. Some people love to drive, and he was just crazy about doing that sort of thing.
Never saw him yawn on the stand either.
I don't know. I was too busy. Yeah.
